To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) countercyclical aggregate demand policies are not neutral to long-run outcomes; (2) countercyclicality in Latin America and in the Caribbean is characterized by a shorter and less intense expansion phase; (3) short-run fluctuations have a significant impact on long-run outcomes; and (4) countercyclicity in Latin America and Caribbean economies is characterized by a financial amplifier effect, with credit recovering later than the real economy.
the cycle and the trend are interdependent, and countercyclical and structural policies are complementary and mutually reinforcing.

the business cycle in Latin America and Caribbean is characterized by: short and weak expansions; a strong and prolonged contraction phase; a long duration and high intensity of recessions; a strong and protracted recovery phase; and a weak and protracted expansion phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the design and implementation of countercyclicity affects long-run growth trends.
how the cycle and trend of economies are interdependent and how this interdependence shapes the design and implementation of countercyclic policies.
the design and implementation of countercyc- ical policy in Latin America and Caribbean economies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
countercyclicity is a necessary but not sufficient condition for long-run macroeconomic performance.
the countercyclical stance should be more active and more effective than it has been in the past, and that the active strategy of development should be more countercyclical.
countercyclicality must be a long-run strategy, not a short-run policy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
countercyclicity is a key component of a development strategy, but that countercyclicality should be designed and implemented in a development-friendly manner.
countercyclicality should not only be about the cycle but also about the trend.
macroeconomic policy should focus on the long-run growth of an economy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design and implementation of countercyc-lical policy in Latin America and Caribbean economies must take into account the specificities of the region’s business cycle.
the design of countercyclic policies must be based on the understanding that they are not neutral to long-run growth.
countercyclicity is a long-run strategy.
